title: Tidy the #679 review leftovers: managed-remedy docblocks, discriminating tests, init docs, JSDoc, per-row re-read
description: Non-blocking findings 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 from the Opus re-review of PR #679 at cbbfd7d5, recorded verbatim on QCLI-532. Findings 5 and 7 are routed to opum-doc by the lead and are not this task. (1) agent-plugins.ts docblock above managedScopeRemedy says "One string for installed and disabled alike" and test/qcli381 comment says "One string for both states"; both are false since fee1c15e. Confirm with lore-cli (LCLI-766) that its disabled managed row prints the same (a9) 7 text before calling the pair byte-identical. (2) test "a non-regular settings file is not read" uses a directory, so EISDIR is caught anyway and removing isFile() leaves it green; add a whitespace-padded valid file past maxPluginOutputBytes expecting no override (a 1 MiB cap test), and a FIFO case for isFile. (3) quest init also calls detectQuestPlugin, so its JSON carries plugins.claude.override and the --scope local remedy; the CHANGELOG names only agents --check. (4) two consecutive JSDoc blocks in main.ts put the renderAgentCheckLines doc above overrideCollaboratorClause. (6) the adapter re-stats and re-reads both settings files once per listed claude plugin though only the opum-quest row is consumed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The managedScopeRemedy docblock and the qcli381 comment no longer claim one string for both states
A test goes red when the isFile() guard is removed and another when the 1 MiB cap is removed
The init surface carrying plugins.claude.override and its remedy is documented in the CHANGELOG or help
Each JSDoc block sits above the symbol it describes
The settings files are read for the opum-quest row only

implementationNotes: DEC-238 (a11), opum-ai/opum-doc#1372 (merged be51f16, .quest/planning.json, DEC-238 outcome), relayed by the leader 2026-10-25, the ruling on the #679 review findings 5 and 7, verbatim: PLACEMENT (finding 5): no change. Byte identity between the CLIs covers the override line own bytes, not where it sits in the surrounding output, which already differs by design: lore prints plugin-claude <state> record lines, and quest prints its payload dump and keeps its verdict word ((a8)). The one ordering rule is (a9) ORDER, override line before the remedy. lore places it after its state line, and quest prepends it before the dump. Both meet the rule, and quest indexOf test is the right test of it. PRECEDENCE (finding 7): the state each CLI reports for the Claude plugin is the EFFECTIVE one under Claude own precedence, managed over local over project over user. An explicit true in a higher scope beats a false in a lower one, and the user scope is included. So a project-file or local true over a user-scope false reads as enabled in this checkout, with no override line and no remedy. Measure first: run claude plugin list --json with a project-file true over a user-scope false, in a scratch project with its own config dir, never the operator user settings. If the listing already reports the effective state, record the measurement and change nothing. If it does not, derive the state from the settings files, with a test both ways. Both CLIs get the same rule: quest-cli under QCLI-534, lore-cli with LCLI-766. Low priority, and it holds nothing. Do not start the measurement until the plan schedules QCLI-534. Also: lore-cli recorded the managed-row split as LCLI-766 ninth criterion (opum-ai/lore-cli#682, 44c1a93); finding 1 check against lore cites it.
